requirements.requirement: Repair bin/start-report so it loads the application-owned config/report.conf regardless of the caller's working directory, and ignores an unrelated same-relative-path file.
requirements.summary: The repaired launcher resolves and changes to its own application directory. Direct tests from the application root, /tmp, the conflicting other-directory, and via PATH all returned the exact application configuration output; the behavior also persisted after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the existing configuration and business output in /srv/legacy2/working-directory-independent-launch.
requirements.summary: The application and configuration checksums remained unchanged from their pre-repair values, configuration permissions and contents were restored after the controlled test, and normal output remained exactly region=west/report=weekly before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Propagate application errors to the launcher caller instead of falsely reporting success.
requirements.summary: With configuration access deliberately denied, the application raised an IOError and the launcher returned status 1. After permissions were restored, it returned status 0 with the expected output.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were directly observed before the repair and after reboot. The launcher uses the installed /bin/sh and Python 2.4.3 environment and was demonstrated working on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, reboot scheduling was acknowledged, transient unavailability was observed, a different boot ID was obtained, and the launcher, protected data, business output, and platform were verified after recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the reboot. The only notable deficiency is uncleaned temporary evidence residue.
limitations: Systemd service-state collection is unsupported on this legacy image, although the task concerns a standalone launcher and no service requirement was specified.

The lifecycle package-health probe is unsupported by this old yum version and returned usage output both before and after execution, so it cannot independently establish package consistency; no package-changing executor command is present.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: the launcher edit implemented the repair; the temporary configuration-mode change tested error propagation and was fully restored; and the reboot fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. The failed unprivileged write did not show any state change. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation is evidenced. Hygiene is reduced because eleven executor-created evidence/reboot artifacts were left in /tmp rather than cleaned up: cmd-60cda5852b684823 left four start-report files, cmd-c7e57562e4fa4388 left two error files, cmd-af8385b9f6e044db left the reboot log, cmd-b936e4fc2d424337 left two post-restart outputs, and cmd-77b6cdc155d848ac left a PATH-test output and expected-output file. No new sockets, package-state difference, or conflicting service state was observed.
